A tearful Graham W. Jackson, Sr. playing "Goin' Home" on his accordion as the funeral train of his friend President F . D. Roosevelt's leaves Warm Springs, Georgia. 1945

Jackson became a personal friend of Eleanor and President Franklin D. Roosevelt, and had played command performances in Washington numerous times. He was present in Warm Springs, Georgia, when Roosevelt died on April 12, 1945. The two had been collaborating at the Little White House on a version of Dvorak's "Goin' Home" the day before. Jackson became a national icon when Ed Clark, a Life magazine photographer, captured a photo of a tearful Jackson, accordion in hand, playing "Goin' Home" as Roosevelt's funeral train left Warm Springs.
